OBLIVION is a software engineering organization. It builds software, AI systems and games with a small group of programmers and a larger group of specialized AI workers.

The programmers set direction, design the architecture, review the work and keep final control. The AI workers write code, run tests, analyze, research, document and review under that direction. Our flagship system, Angra, is the layer that lets several local models work on one objective instead of one model answering one prompt.

Roles are a conceptual grouping. No per-role counts are claimed.

A model generates. Angra coordinates.

Angra is an OBLIVION-built coordination layer for compatible local AI models running through LM Studio and Bionic. One model becomes a worker. Several models become a workforce, with a person in control.

Open the Angra siteTry the simulation

What Angra is

  • A coordination layer between you and the local models you already run.
  • Operator-controlled: you choose which models connect and what they may do.
  • Built to split an objective, route the parts and check the result.

What Angra is not

  • Not an AI model. It does not generate; the models do.
  • Not a hosted service or a distributed network.
  • Not a claim of autonomous operation. A person stays in the loop.
